item.title: Climate disasters deepen food insecurity in the Punjab
item.description: Following devastating floods that destroyed crops in the breadbasket region of India and Pakistan, food insecurity continues to loom large.

item.title: Concrete ocean pledges lacking in countries’ climate plans, say experts
item.description: Ocean-based goals in submitted Nationally Determined Contributions overlook tougher targets including fossil fuel phase-out.

item.title: Deadly floods affect millions across South and Southeast Asia, leaving over $4 billion in loss and damage
item.description: Heavy rainfall across the region was caused by the combination of natural phenomena and climate change but in Indonesia's Sumatra, where the most lives have been lost, the scale of disaster was worsened by deforestation.

item.title: South Korea doubles financial support for renewable projects in 2026 budget
item.description: Seoul will also keep 2026 EV and hydrogen-vehicle subsidies at current levels, halting a long-running policy of annual cuts aimed at nudging the market towards self-sufficiency.

item.title: Plastic pollution is accelerating, but are governments keeping up?
item.description: Plastic waste will soar to unprecedented levels without action, as UN plastics treaty remains elusive.

item.title: Climate ‘loss and damage’ should include supply chain impacts
item.description: Ensuring funds reach countries most in need, quickly and equitably, is climate finance’s biggest challenge.

item.title: Analysis: Why COP30’s ‘tripling adaptation finance’ target is less ambitious than it seems
item.description: One of the headline outcomes to emerge from COP30 was a new target to “at least triple” finance for climate adaptation in developing countries by 2035.

item.title: No evidence that cloud seeding can cut air pollution: experts
item.description: The Delhi government, in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur, recently conducted cloud seeding experiments with the claim of reducing air pollution.

item.title: Taiwan plans first heat emergency drill as elderly heat injuries hit decade high
item.description: The island has also launched a three-tier heat response care system for the elderly in the southern city of Tainan, where heat-related illnesses among older residents have grown fivefold in a decade.

item.title: 'I want others to own sustainability too – but letting go is hard': Golden Agri CSO Anita Neville
item.description: Unless sustainability heads allow other functions to take the lead, ESG will never be fully integrated into a business, the CSO of the world's second-largest palm oil company tells the EB Podcast.
